record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: If D is a downward-closed collection of subsets, is it always true that the alternating sum over its nonempty members is bounded by the total number of positive- and negative-border elements, namely Σ_{∅≠Y∈D} (−1)^{|Y|+1} ≤ |Bd⁺(D)| + |Bd⁻(D)|?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12 For downwards closed collection D we have Σ∅≠Y ∈D (−1)|Y |+1 ≤ |Bd+(D)| + |Bd−(D)|

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $U$ be a finite set, and let $\mathcal{D} \subseteq 2^U$ be a downward-closed family of subsets of $U$ (that is, if $Y \in \mathcal{D}$ and $Z \subseteq Y$, then $Z \in \mathcal{D}$). Define the positive border of $\mathcal{D}$ as
$$\mathrm{Bd}^{+}(\mathcal{D}) = \{Y \in \mathcal{D} : \text{for every } Z \subseteq U \text{ with } Y \subsetneq Z,\ Z \notin \mathcal{D}\},$$
i.e. the maximal elements of $\mathcal{D}$, and the negative border as
$$\mathrm{Bd}^{-}(\mathcal{D}) = \{Y \subseteq U : Y \notin \mathcal{D}\text{ and every proper subset of } Y \text{ is in } \mathcal{D}\},$$
i.e. the minimal subsets of $U$ that do not lie in $\mathcal{D}$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite downward-closed collection $\mathcal{D}$,
$$\sum_{\emptyset \neq Y \in \mathcal{D}} (-1)^{|Y|+1} \;\le\; |\mathrm{Bd}^{+}(\mathcal{D})| + |\mathrm{Bd}^{-}(\mathcal{D})|.$$

The status appears unresolved in publicly indexed literature.
